newsitem.title: UK: IPE oil futures little changed, may test $18.
newsitem.headline: IPE oil futures little changed, may test $18.

text.p: IPE Brent crude and gas oil futures were little changed in early business, but with an air of uncertainty creeping into the market prices are expected to drift down over the morning to test $18 support, traders said.

By 0930 GMT the September Brent contract was trading three cents up at $18.15 a barrel with gas oil unchanged at $163.50 a tonne. "$18 is expected to come under attack today," said GNI Research in there daily report.
But they said there were a number of potential support levels below this at $17.95, $17.85-80, $17.60, $17.45/50 and then $17.30 to slow the pace of any downside.
GNI said the early focus today would be the U.N., which should "rubber stamp" the Iraqi oil sale agreement.
"This is fully expected by the market but there should still be a reaction, since this could actually mean Iraqi oil shipments in the next week or two," they said.
Peter Sceats, analyst at CharTech-MCS, took a neutral to bullish stance short term expecting the uptrend to hold for now.
"The market showed signs of life on the upside last week as the uptrend on the spot month continuation and weekly charts stayed intact and a mini double bottom was posted," Sceats said.
Sceats defines the reconfiguration of a six-week uptrend on the spot month continuation chart that takes into account the mini double bottom at $17.80 from Monday and Tuesday of last week.
"Join the $17.32 (June 11) and $17.49 (June 20) lows with $17.80 (double bottom) and you will see what we believe the most important short term technical pattern on the chart".
